pageCache.pageTitle: Vision, Mission, Values - John Keats Primary School
pageCache.text:
Vision, Mission, Values
Our vision is that John Keats Primary School will act as a positive catalyst for change and improvement within its community.
It will develop to be an outstanding, all-through school for children in the Bermondsey area that will fulfil their educational aspirations and dreams and meet complex pastoral needs.
Serving our community is a core feature of our vision. Geographically, we aim to establish ourselves as an outstanding provider of education with a view to spreading our provision across the local area. We plan to work collaboratively and build strong working relationships locally, nationally and internationally with other academies, schools and local nursery provision.
John Keats Primary School will be founded on the solid educational and pedagogical principles that have made John Donne Primary such a success. We are confident that we can provide academic results as evidence of our capability to replicate our success to date.
We envisage John Keats Primary School as a school where every child/student becomes:
To improve on our previous best
To develop self-discipline and a positive self-image.
literate and numerate with good technology skills
a problem-solver, collaborator, leader and resilient

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome from the Headteacher - John Keats Primary School
pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Headteacher
Welcome to John Keats Primary School.
Our high expectations ensure each child makes exceptional progress during their time with us.
Every child at John Keats is cherished; and our school community, supported by a committed and devoted staff team, value our dedication to their child and family.
It is our belief that every child has limitless potential and we are passionate about unlocking this to develop their confidence, uncover their talents and nurture their aspirations, empowering them to build the foundations of their success.
We understand the importance of providing every child with a forward-thinking and aspirational experience, enabling them to take their first successful steps on a pathway that they will forge for the rest of their lives. Our inspiring curriculum and dedicated team of staff not only supports pupils academically but focuses on developing the whole child as these opportunities extend beyond the classroom. We offer the widest range of enrichment experiences: extensive clubs, a range of stimulating school trips and visits alongside the use of our excellent indoor and outdoor activity facilities.
Due to our excellent location, the richness of our offer is also enhanced through partnerships, networks and collaborative projects with other organisations, providing exciting opportunities and allowing for personal development for both pupils and staff.
Our success lies in the close and safe community that flourishes here at John Keats, and the excellent relationships that exist between staff, pupils, parents and the local community.
Matt Rose

Admissions
John Keats Primary School is a 2-form entry Primary school in the Communitas Education Trust (The Trust), situated in Bermondsey.
The educational provision at John Keats Primary School will significantly improve our pupils’ life chances. Pupils will receive outstanding teaching across a range of subjects in a broad and balanced curriculum and will leave the school having achieved well and been prepared for secondary school.
Pupil Admission Number (PAN)
John Keats Primary School has an admission number of 60 for entry in the Reception year.
How to Apply
Reception
If you have a child who is starting reception in September 2025, then please come along and meet us at one of our Reception open days.
Full details of our dates and times can be found at the end of this page.
Alternatively, you can contact the school office on 020 3955 8176 should you have any questions or need to arrange a virtual Q&A session. Applications for reception places are made by completing Southwark’s on-line application form available:

Admissions policySupport and advice about applications is available at the school.
Appeals: all appeals should be sent back directly to the school office. Parents have the right to appeal even if they have no grounds to do so.

Curriculum
What do pupils learn at John Keats?
“Teachers have good subject knowledge and explain things clearly to pupils. Across the curriculum, they make sure that pupils have regular opportunities to recall and revisit prior learning. Teachers know their pupils’ needs well… they find out exactly what pupils know and can do, and then build pupils’ knowledge in a progressive manner. The curriculum is implemented consistently well, and teaching introduces new knowledge in clear, manageable steps.” Ofsted
At John Keats, we teach the UK National Primary Curriculum through six key themes. Adopted from the International Baccalaureate, children study each of these themes for a half term. They return to them each year, deepening their knowledge and making links between content and subjects. Through them they explore the foundation subjects and make links to their Reading and Writing lessons too. This thematic approach enables children to learn in a purposeful, adaptive way, which provides them with real-world skills and knowledge.
Curriculum Overview
Autumn 1 - Who Are We
Autumn 2 - Where We Are In Place and Time
Spring 1 - How Do We Express Ourselves
Spring 2 - How Does Our World Work
Summer 1 - How Do We Organise Ourselves
Summer 2 - How Do We Share The Planet

Nursery
John Keats Nursery is a fun, loving environment in which your child can begin their school life.
We believe that Nursery is the key starting point to a child’s educational journey and we ensure this is supported with a fully qualified teacher. Our learning is all focused on learning through play. We believe that Nursery is a great place to build on children's social and self-care skills. We want to give children confidence in themselves and hence help them to be curious and independent learners. We encourage learning as a class group, small groups and on an individual level. We have a theme to our learning which changes every half term and then within this we focus on a story book a week on which we base a lot of our activities. Here at John Keats, we love getting messy in nursery and do lots of arts and crafts. Children have access to water, sand, mud, painting, sticking, playdoh and all sorts of other hands-on activities every day. We also encourage physical development with lots of time in the big playground playing games, riding bikes and scooters and having fun. Being part of school means we continuously access lots of other extra activities and be involved in school wide projects.
We offer both Full time (30 Hours) and Part time (15 Hours) per week. Children who attend 15 Hours per week are free to attend and we offer flexibility with the sessions using their 15 hours of funding.
For full time hours (08:40 - 3:15pm) we offer 30 hours free childcare places if parents meet the eligibility criteria. We also offer the option of paying for additional sessions if parents do not meet the eligibility criteria for 30 hours free childcare. Additional session prices are currently £17.50 per session but are subject to change by the trust from time to time due to inflation. We will give parents a minimum of a term notice if this changes.

Safeguarding Team
John Keats Primary School is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment.
We have a number of policies and procedures in place that contribute to our safeguarding commitment, including our Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy, which can be viewed in the Policies section.
Sometimes we may need to share information and work in partnership with other agencies when there are concerns about a child's welfare. We will ensure that our concerns about our pupils are discussed with their family first unless we have reason to believe that such a move would be contrary to the child's welfare.
Our Designated Safeguarding and Child Protection Lead is Matt Rose, and our Deputies are Georgia Denny, Evie Littlechild, Cherilee Oldacre, Maisie Philips, George Preston and Sofia Gumpert.
Looked After Children: Matt Rose
Multi-Agency Safeguarding Hub (MASH)
If you think that a child or young person under the age of 18 years old, who lives in the borough, is being abused or neglected, contact the MASH Team using the contact details below. Outside of office hours and at weekends and public holidays contact the 'out of hours contact' service on 020 7525 5000. If you are seriously concerned about a child's immediate safety, dial 999.
Not all concerns raised about a child will automatically lead to a child protection investigation. Less serious concerns may lead to a more general assessment of need and the provision of services or the offer of advice and information.
T: 020 7525 1921mash@southwark.gov.uk Southwark Out of Hours Duty Service (EDT) phone number below, (between 5.00pm and 8.30am Monday to Sunday):
Emergencies only: 020 7525 5000
Southwark LADO (overall responsibility for safeguarding in the borough)
Local Authority Designated Officer (LADO): Tel: 020 7525 0689
Or tel: 07943 076608
eva.simcock@southwark.gov.uk qau.safeguarding@southwark.gov.uk
Parent/Carer Helpers
If you plan to help in school you need to contact the school to apply for a DBS certificate or renew your certificate when the three year period has expired. Please contact the school office for further information.
